account: Representative Jennifer Wexton of Virginia was diagnosed in 2023 with progressive supranuclear palsy. ElevenLabs approached her office in spring 2024, and her staff sent over an hour of old recordings. The Associated Press reported that ElevenLabs built the voice from recordings of her congressional speeches and public appearances. On 25 July 2024 she gave a House floor speech for Disability Pride Month. She used an augmentative and alternative communication device playing an AI-generated clone of her voice. The Congressional Record has her saying that progressive supranuclear palsy “has robbed me of my ability to use my full voice”. She said that hearing the recreation was “the most beautiful thing I had ever heard, and I cried tears of joy”. In an interview that Politico published on 9 September 2024, she said that the model was ready in a couple of days and that she first used it at the White House. She also said that it can sound too formal for conversation and needs a strong signal. Andrew Zaleski of Washingtonian spoke with her through the cloned voice for a feature published on 31 December 2024, and he reports that she was still using the voice as her term ended. The Office of the House Historian, which published her oral history on 27 March 2026, states that she was the first Member to speak on the House floor using this type of assistive technology.

ai_role.statement: The cloned voice is the AI output. Wexton wrote the content and the AAC device played it. A generic synthetic voice would also have carried the words, so the AI-specific benefit is the restoration of her own voice.

fields.headline: Lawmaker who lost her speech addresses the House in her cloned voice
fields.title: Rep. Jennifer Wexton addresses the House with an AI clone of her own voice after progressive supranuclear palsy took her speech

fields.account: Representative Jennifer Wexton of Virginia was diagnosed in 2023 with progressive supranuclear palsy. ElevenLabs approached her office in spring 2024, and her staff sent over an hour of old recordings. The Associated Press reported that ElevenLabs built the voice from recordings of her congressional speeches and public appearances. On 25 July 2024 she gave a House floor speech for Disability Pride Month. She used an augmentative and alternative communication device playing an AI-generated clone of her voice. The Congressional Record has her saying that progressive supranuclear palsy “has robbed me of my ability to use my full voice”. She said that hearing the recreation was “the most beautiful thing I had ever heard, and I cried tears of joy”. In an interview that Politico published on 9 September 2024, she said that the model was ready in a couple of days and that she first used it at the White House. She also said that it can sound too formal for conversation and needs a strong signal. Andrew Zaleski of Washingtonian spoke with her through the cloned voice for a feature published on 31 December 2024, and he reports that she was still using the voice as her term ended. The Office of the House Historian, which published her oral history on 27 March 2026, states that she was the first Member to speak on the House floor using this type of assistive technology.

purpose: ElevenLabs voice cloning is built to reproduce a person's voice from recordings. Restoring her own voice for speech was that purpose.

ratings.reason: A legislator who lost intelligible speech regained the ability to address the House in a voice recognizably her own. She told the Associated Press that it was “more me than I ever could have hoped I could hear again”.

The House Historian states that she was the first Member to speak on the House floor using this type of assistive technology. No source reports a realized outcome for society that followed from that first.
